stages.title: Establish the scene
stages.body: Two synthetic vessels follow fixed tracks. Start in the overview, then use the bridge camera to compare perspectives. This is a player demonstration, not a navigational exercise.

stages.title: Observe relative motion
stages.body: Watch how the apparent position of the other vessel changes. Toggle the track overlay to connect the 3D view with the route geometry.

stages.title: Change your perspective
stages.body: Select either vessel and switch to Bridge. The camera follows its position and heading. Pause at any instant to inspect the scene.

stages.title: Review the encounter
stages.body: Scrub back to an earlier moment. The same time always produces the same vessel positions. Rule explanations will be added after the source material is reviewed.

stages.title: Before the turn
stages.body: Atlas begins on a straight track. Nord follows a separate fixed track. This scene demonstrates the animation system only; it does not establish COLREG duties.

stages.title: An authored course change
stages.body: Atlas starts the scripted turn. Its heading and position are sampled from the same timeline. Use 0.5× speed to examine the transition.

stages.title: Inspect the movement
stages.body: Switch between the overhead and bridge views. Heading arrows show orientation; the visible track records movement up to the current time.

stages.title: Replay and compare
stages.body: The turn is complete. Jump between the steps or scrub backwards to review. Once the book arrives, reviewed scenario data will replace these synthetic examples.

conditions: Rule 1 establishes where the regulations apply.
Rule 2 preserves responsibility for compliance, ordinary seamanship and special circumstances.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Rule 1 establishes where the regulations apply. Rule 2 preserves responsibility for compliance, ordinary seamanship and special circumstances.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: The Rules apply to vessels on the high seas and connected navigable waters, while responsibility still includes precautions required by ordinary seamanship and special circumstances.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Use this scene as a reminder to assess the full circumstances and applicable duties.

conditions: Status follows the Rule 3 definitions, not casual hull labels.
A vessel can be underway without making way through the water.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Status follows the Rule 3 definitions, not casual hull labels. A vessel can be underway without making way through the water.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Terms such as vessel, power-driven, sailing, underway and making way determine which later duties fit the facts.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Conduct in any condition of visibility
subtitle: Rule 4 · open

conditions: Rule 4 introduces Section I.
Look-out, safe speed and risk assessment remain relevant in clear and restricted visibility.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Rule 4 introduces Section I. Look-out, safe speed and risk assessment remain relevant in clear and restricted visibility.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Rules 4–10 form the conduct requirements that apply in any condition of visibility.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The vessels can be observed visually from one another.
A radar-only encounter in fog is treated under Rule 19 instead.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The vessels can be observed visually from one another. A radar-only encounter in fog is treated under Rule 19 instead.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: The steering and sailing rules in Section II apply when vessels are in sight of one another.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: Rule 5 applies at all times.
The look-out supports a full appraisal of the situation and risk of collision.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Rule 5 applies at all times. The look-out supports a full appraisal of the situation and risk of collision.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Visual scanning, hearing and available instruments contribute to a continuing appraisal.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Safe speed depends on the circumstances
subtitle: Rule 6 · open

conditions: Safe speed is contextual rather than a universal number.
The vessel must retain scope for proper and effective action.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Safe speed is contextual rather than a universal number. The vessel must retain scope for proper and effective action.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Traffic, manoeuvrability, visibility and environmental limits must be weighed together.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: Use all available means to determine risk.
Scanty information is not a sound basis for an assumption.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Use all available means to determine risk. Scanty information is not a sound basis for an assumption.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A target that remains on nearly the same compass bearing while range closes is a classic collision-risk cue.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Risk can exist with bearing change
subtitle: Rule 7 · open

conditions: Do not treat bearing change as a guarantee of safety.
Assess the target’s size, range and geometry.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Do not treat bearing change as a guarantee of safety. Assess the target’s size, range and geometry.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A large vessel, tow or close-range target can create risk even when the bearing changes appreciably.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Action should be positive and apparent
subtitle: Rule 8 · open

conditions: Action should accord with good seamanship.
Monitor the result until finally past and clear.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Action should accord with good seamanship. Monitor the result until finally past and clear.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A clear alteration made in ample time is easier for the other vessel to detect than a succession of small changes.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Slowing as part of collision avoidance
subtitle: Rule 8 · open

conditions: The depicted speed change is illustrative.
Rule 8 does not prescribe one stopping distance or timeline.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The depicted speed change is illustrative. Rule 8 does not prescribe one stopping distance or timeline.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Reducing speed, stopping or reversing propulsion may be appropriate when the circumstances require it.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: This lesson assumes both are power-driven and in sight.
The geometry is illustrative; no universal trigger distance is implied.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: This lesson assumes both are power-driven and in sight. The geometry is illustrative; no universal trigger distance is implied.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: When reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses involve risk, each alters course to starboard.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Crossing vessel on the starboard side
subtitle: Rules 15, 16 · open

conditions: Both vessels are power-driven and in sight.
Give-way action remains subject to the full circumstances.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Both vessels are power-driven and in sight. Give-way action remains subject to the full circumstances.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: The vessel that has the other on her starboard side keeps out of the way and, if circumstances admit, avoids crossing ahead.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Crossing encounter viewed from the stand-on vessel
subtitle: Rules 15, 17 · open

conditions: Both vessels are power-driven and in sight.
Stand-on status still requires watchful monitoring.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Both vessels are power-driven and in sight. Stand-on status still requires watchful monitoring.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: The mirrored view identifies why the vessel seeing the other to port is initially the stand-on vessel.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The faster vessel approaches from more than 22.5° abaft the beam.
Passing side does not transfer the overtaking duty.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The faster vessel approaches from more than 22.5° abaft the beam. Passing side does not transfer the overtaking duty.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: An overtaking vessel keeps out of the way until finally past and clear, whichever side it uses.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The faster vessel is approaching from the overtaking sector.
Clearance and timing are illustrative.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The faster vessel is approaching from the overtaking sector. Clearance and timing are illustrative.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Passing on the other side leaves the overtaking vessel’s duty unchanged.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The 22.5° line defines the overtaking sector.
The scene exaggerates lateral spacing so the boundary is readable.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The 22.5° line defines the overtaking sector. The scene exaggerates lateral spacing so the boundary is readable.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A target near the sector boundary demands careful classification; if in doubt, treat the vessel as overtaking.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: Both vessels are under sail and in sight.
Wind is shown as an illustrative direction.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Both vessels are under sail and in sight. Wind is shown as an illustrative direction.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: With wind on different sides, the vessel with wind on the port side keeps out of the way.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Sailing vessels on the same tack
subtitle: Rule 12 · open

conditions: Both vessels are under sail on the same tack.
Relative windward and leeward positions are the teaching focus.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Both vessels are under sail on the same tack. Relative windward and leeward positions are the teaching focus.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: With wind on the same side, the windward vessel keeps out of the way of the leeward vessel.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Uncertain tack of the windward vessel
subtitle: Rule 12 · open

conditions: Sails and lights may be difficult to interpret in practice.
Uncertainty is part of the rule condition.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Sails and lights may be difficult to interpret in practice. Uncertainty is part of the rule condition.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A port-tack vessel that cannot determine whether the windward vessel has wind on her port or starboard side keeps out of the way.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Stand-on stage: keep course and speed
subtitle: Rule 17 · open

conditions: Risk of collision exists and the vessels are in sight.
The stage changes if the give-way vessel does not act.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: Risk of collision exists and the vessels are in sight. The stage changes if the give-way vessel does not act.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: At the initial stage, the stand-on vessel maintains course and speed while monitoring the give-way vessel.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: This is the intermediate Rule 17 stage.
Any action must be assessed in the actual circumstances.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: This is the intermediate Rule 17 stage. Any action must be assessed in the actual circumstances.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: When it becomes apparent that the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action, the stand-on vessel may act by her manoeuvre alone.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Stand-on stage: shall take best action
subtitle: Rule 17 · open

conditions: This is the later compulsory stage.
The scene does not prescribe a universal manoeuvre.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: This is the later compulsory stage. The scene does not prescribe a universal manoeuvre.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: When collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel’s action alone, the stand-on vessel takes the action that will best aid avoidance.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The sailing vessel is genuinely under sail.
Rule 18 must be read with Rules 9, 10 and 13.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The sailing vessel is genuinely under sail. Rule 18 must be read with Rules 9, 10 and 13.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A power-driven vessel underway keeps out of the way of a sailing vessel, subject to the Rules’ stated exceptions.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The fishing vessel’s gear restricts manoeuvrability.
A vessel merely carrying fishing gear is not automatically engaged in fishing.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The fishing vessel’s gear restricts manoeuvrability. A vessel merely carrying fishing gear is not automatically engaged in fishing.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Except where Rules 9, 10 and 13 otherwise require, a power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of a vessel engaged in fishing.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The NUC vessel cannot manoeuvre as required by the Rules.
Shapes and lights, not hull type, establish status.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The NUC vessel cannot manoeuvre as required by the Rules. Shapes and lights, not hull type, establish status.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Except where Rules 9, 10 and 13 otherwise require, this power-driven vessel underway shall keep out of the way of the vessel not under command.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Vessel restricted in ability to manoeuvre
subtitle: Rule 18 · open

conditions: The restriction arises from the nature of the vessel’s work.
The depicted work area and spacing are illustrative.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The restriction arises from the nature of the vessel’s work. The depicted work area and spacing are illustrative.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Other vessels keep out of the way of a RAM vessel so far as possible, with the hierarchy and exceptions considered together.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The constrained vessel is power-driven and severely restricted in her ability to deviate from her course by her draught relative to available depth and width.
This status depends on the particular navigable water.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The constrained vessel is power-driven and severely restricted in her ability to deviate from her course by her draught relative to available depth and width. This status depends on the particular navigable water.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A vessel other than one not under command or restricted in ability to manoeuvre shall, if circumstances admit, avoid impeding the safe passage of a vessel constrained by her draught and exhibiting the Rule 28 signals.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Keep near the channel’s starboard limit
subtitle: Rule 9 · channel

conditions: The waterway is treated as a narrow channel.
The illustrated lane offset is not a rule-defined distance.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The waterway is treated as a narrow channel. The illustrated lane offset is not a rule-defined distance.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A vessel proceeding along a narrow channel keeps as near to the outer limit on her starboard side as is safe and practicable.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The through vessel can safely navigate only within the channel.
This schematic timing is illustrative and does not demonstrate that the shown crossing is non-impeding.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The through vessel can safely navigate only within the channel. This schematic timing is illustrative and does not demonstrate that the shown crossing is non-impeding.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A crossing vessel must not impede a vessel that can safely navigate only within the channel.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The channel limits free manoeuvre.
Agreement does not relieve the overtaking vessel of her Rule 13 duty.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The channel limits free manoeuvre. Agreement does not relieve the overtaking vessel of her Rule 13 duty.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: When overtaking can occur only if the vessel being overtaken cooperates, the prescribed sound-signal exchange communicates intention and agreement.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The bend obstructs sight of approaching traffic.
Rule 34(e) supplies the prolonged bend signal and reply.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The bend obstructs sight of approaching traffic. Rule 34(e) supplies the prolonged bend signal and reply.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: Near a bend where vessels may be obscured, navigate with particular alertness, sound one prolonged blast and answer a heard bend signal with one prolonged blast.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The marked route is a traffic separation scheme.
The joining angle is illustrative, not a numeric rule threshold.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The marked route is a traffic separation scheme. The joining angle is illustrative, not a numeric rule threshold.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A vessel joining a lane does so at as small an angle to the general direction of traffic flow as practicable.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The vessel is crossing rather than joining the lane.
The rule concerns heading, while current may change track over ground.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The vessel is crossing rather than joining the lane. The rule concerns heading, while current may change track over ground.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: When obliged to cross a traffic lane, a vessel crosses on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the traffic flow.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The vessels are not in sight of one another.
The contact is detected by radar in restricted visibility.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The vessels are not in sight of one another. The contact is detected by radar in restricted visibility.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: A radar-only contact forward of the beam calls for early assessment and caution about alterations to port.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

title: Restricted visibility: contact abeam or abaft
subtitle: Rule 19 · open

conditions: The vessels are not in sight of one another.
Relative position is established by systematic radar observation.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The vessels are not in sight of one another. Relative position is established by systematic radar observation.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: For a radar-only contact abeam or abaft the beam, Rule 19 cautions against altering toward the vessel.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.

conditions: The signal is heard apparently forward of the beam.
No universal distance or response time is implied.

stages.title: Identify the conditions
stages.body: The signal is heard apparently forward of the beam. No universal distance or response time is implied.

stages.title: Apply the rule
stages.body: On hearing an apparently forward fog signal, reduce to the minimum speed at which course can be kept and, if necessary, take all way off while navigating with extreme caution.

stages.title: Check the outcome
stages.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.
